newsitem.title: UKRAINE: SOCCER-UKRAINE PREPARED TO PLAY IN ALBANIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UKRAINE PREPARED TO PLAY IN ALBANIA.

text.p: Ukraine are prepared to play their World Cup qualifier in Albania later this month despite worsening unrest in the Balkan country, a top Ukranian soccer official said on Tuesday.
"We will play there," president of Ukraine's Football Federation Valery Pustovoitenko told reporters. "The organisers guarantee the necessary protection and order during the match."
He said Ukraine's foreign ministry had received similar assurances from Albanian embassies in Russia and Poland. Tirana has no official mission in Kiev.
Pustovoiteno said federation officials would visit Tirana later this month to check safety standards there.

FIFA said earlier in the day it was looking into the possibility of alternative venues for the Albania-Ukraine group nine match, scheduled for March 29, and Albania's home tie with Germany four days later.
With Albania teetering on the brink of civil war following the collapse of a pyramid savings schemes, it may be forced to play both matches at a neutral site.
The FIFA World Cup organising committee is to discuss the situation and make a decision before the end of the week.
"It's become clear that it's not possible to play matches there (at the moment)," FIFA spokesman Keith Cooper said.
"We have two options. We can postpone the games but there is no certainty that the situation will settle down. The other option is to play on the same dates at neutral grounds.
